# Afterword: What You Built, and Where Next {.unnumbered .backmatter #sec-afterword}

If you followed the book through, you built two projects. The London guide became a web page, a Word
document, a PDF, a dashboard, a partner brief with its email, a flyer and a published website, and
optionally slides, an e-book, a square advert and a white paper. The water analysis became exploratory
pages, a report in Word and PDF, council slides in two formats, a blog post and a published website, and
optionally an e-book, a dashboard and a paper. Each started from plain text and data, and each rebuilds
with one command.

More useful than the outputs are the habits that made them trustworthy, because they transfer to any
project:

- **Compute every number.** A typed number goes stale; a computed one updates and can be traced back to
  its data.
- **Write the rules down.** A short `AGENTS.md` keeps an assistant to the project's scope, data rules and
  commands across sessions, and is a checklist for you too.
- **Compute once, publish many.** When an analysis feeds several outputs, put it in one script and have
  every output read its results.
- **Predict, then check.** Before a rebuild, say what should change; afterwards, check that it did.
- **Say what a result does not show.** Descriptive comparisons deserve descriptive sentences, every time
  they are published.
- **Catch up rather than flounder.** A known-good state to return to, a checkpoint or a commit, turns being
  stuck into a two-minute detour.

For your own work, start with the output your readers already ask for, usually a report, and make it
computed and reproducible before adding formats. The second format is where the approach starts to repay
the setup; the first change to the data is where it pays for itself.

## Where next {.unnumbered}

- Quarto's [Guide](https://quarto.org/docs/guide/) covers everything this book used and much it did not:
  books like this one, manuscripts, interactive documents and more output formats (checked 2026-10-30).
- [Dashboards](https://quarto.org/docs/dashboards/), [Typst](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/typst.html)
  and [publishing to GitHub Pages](https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/github-pages.html) are the official
  references for the three areas readers usually extend first (checked 2026-10-30).
- The workshop's slides, examples and checkpoints are at
  <https://github.com/project-delphi/quarto-workshop>; the slides themselves are at
  <https://project-delphi.github.io/quarto-workshop/>.
